dedupe_keys.name: instructions to apply tornadonet to 2011 joplin tornado and 2021 mayfield tornado datasets

description: Tuan Tran, Abdullah Braik and Maria Koliou applied TornadoNET to housing-recovery imagery from the 2011 Joplin tornado and the 2021 Mayfield tornado. The Joplin analysis covers observations from 2011 to 2016, using about 12,000 parcel-level samples labelled as uninhabited, empty, rebuilding or rebuilt. Training and validation were separated geographically. About thirty Mayfield samples per recovery state provided a separate test. The authors report an F1 score of 82.1 percent and inference time of 0.13 seconds per frame for the selected CNN-LSTM model. These are provider-reported results, not independently reproduced findings. The case demonstrates housing-recovery assessment with GIS toolboxes and deep learning. DesignSafe offers public repository access at no stated charge under Open Data Commons Attribution. The separately catalogued TornadoNET software is the related model; file execution and generalisation to other communities remain unverified.
